mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week trend of increasing retail and recreation mobility will continue, driving further recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as reopening progresses.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If workplace mobility continues its recovery and surpasses a -40% threshold, it indicates a significant return to offices, which will boost adjacent retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -40% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in residential mobility combined with an increase in parks mobility suggests people are increasingly leaving their homes for outdoor activities, which will spill over into retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to decrease and PARKS continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If local policies continue to ease, the observed recovery in transit station mobility will accelerate, indicating increased public transport usage that directly correlates with higher retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Transit station mobility continues to recover, but RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in grocery and pharmacy visits, indicating increased essential outings, will translate into a general increase in out-of-home activity, boosting retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues its upward trend, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If the recent slowdown in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recovery persists or reverses, it indicates a pause in return-to-office trends, which will negatively impact retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT week-on-week change becomes negative
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT week-on-week change becomes negative, but RETAIL_REC continues to increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If residential mobility falls below 20% from baseline, it signifies a critical mass of people spending less time at home, directly increasing the potential for retail and recreation visits over the next one week.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 20%, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: As warmer weather encourages more outdoor activities, the sustained increase in parks mobility will draw people out of their homes, leading to increased incidental retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: Parks mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next two weeks.
